author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-scope decision, explicitly flagged in the parent JMAP-sgrr epic's confidence section: 'the convention is used across the whole workspace, including jmap-jscalendar-types; this is closer to all of the workspace contexts fields than a single-crate issue.'

Quick survey:
- jmap-jscontact-types: 14 contexts fields + Phone.features + Relation.relation = 16 sites.
- jmap-jscalendar-types: Participant.roles, Location.linkIds, RecurrenceRule excluded etc. — needs survey (RFC 8984 has similar set-as-map idiom).
- jmap-contacts-types ContactCard: top-level keywords / members / addressBookIds maps.
- jmap-calendars-types: CalendarEvent.participants / keywords / etc.
- Several more across mail-types, chat-types, etc.

Three plausible answers:

  (a) Workspace-wide migration to HashSet<String> + 10-line set-as-map serde adapter (canonical-template approach: change jmap-mail-types first, propagate to every sibling). Breaking change to every crate, large coordinated release. Sole consumer of the adapter would be these fields, so we'd vendor the adapter in jmap-types.

  (b) Crate-by-crate migration starting with jmap-jscontact-types. Creates canonical-template divergence per workspace AGENTS.md until the sweep completes. Each *-types release becomes breaking; the kit's published 0.x versions drift apart for the duration.

  (c) Status quo + workspace AGENTS.md note: the HashMap<String, bool> set-as-map shape is permitted by the spec wire form and accepted across the workspace; callers are responsible for sending value=true (per RFC 9553 §1.5.1 et al.) when constructing wire objects. Document the contract; don't change the type.

Recommendation: option (c) for now. Rationale:
  - Breaking-API cost across ~30 crates is high for a defensive-typing improvement that the wire format already permits.
  - The parent JMAP-sgrr review epic confidence section listed sgrr.18 as a specifically-flagged 'all-of-workspace' concern — not something to spike in one crate.
  - Workspace AGENTS.md already documents the contexts shape implicitly via the Sloppy-Value / extras-preservation policy; an explicit set-as-map subsection would make the contract visible without breaking anything.
  - If (a) is preferred, the right entry point is a fresh workspace-level epic that starts with the canonical sibling jmap-mail-types (or jmap-types if the adapter lives there) and propagates per the canonical-template rule.

If you pick (a) or (b), file a fresh workspace-level epic — not as a JMAP-sgrr.18.* child, because the review scope is jscontact-types only.

If you pick (c), close this with reason citing the workspace-wide scope concern and add a workspace AGENTS.md note documenting the set-as-map idiom contract.
